audits.text:
## 3ee8849ee1ec

**Reproduced color-role shortcut — current normal generation only uses color 4,
while all canonical inputs use color 2.** Pinned generator SHA-256:
`25090e8a71ea517283a492092f71ca9a2fb5d942900e0f4cafd2db244156a1aa`;
canonical rule hash: `8ced42aabbca`.

Across 64 normal draws (the same seed/index/difficulty schedule), every validated
input's nonzero palette was exactly `{4}`. A rival that treats only color 4 as
markers and fills their bounding box with 8 matched the real Racket output on
**64/64** draws. See
`checks/audit/3ee8849ee1ec/generated_shortcut_fit.json` and
`generated_racket.json`.

Canonical train pair 0 is an exact counterexample: its four markers are color 2.
The real rule fills a `5x5` cyan rectangle; the color-4-only rival returns an
empty grid, producing 25 differing cells. The current validator rejects this
canonical input with `expected >=2 color-4 corner cells, found 0`. Exact input,
outputs, hashes, command, validator result, and differing coordinates are in
`checks/audit/3ee8849ee1ec/counterexample.json`; the supported apply receipt is
`checks/audit/3ee8849ee1ec/racket.json`.

The canonical counterexample is intentionally outside the generator's documented
normal domain because that domain itself hardcodes the wrong source color. The
module summary also describes a hollow color-4 outline, whereas the selected
Racket authority paints a solid color-8 rectangle. No fix was made as required
by the audit assignment.
